The '''2024–25 season''' was the 138th season in the history of [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], the club's 33rd in the [[Premier League]], and their 50th consecutive—and 100th overall—season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. The club competed in the [[2024–25 Premier League|Premier League]], the [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]], the [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]], and the [[2024 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]]. It marked the first full season since [[2004–05 Manchester United F.C. season|2004–05]] in which the [[Glazer family]] did not oversee football operations, following the sale of a 27.7% stake to [[Jim Ratcliffe|Sir Jim Ratcliffe]] in February 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Manchester United plc and Trawlers Ltd Announce the Successful Completion of Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Minority Investment |url=https://www.ineos.com/news/ineos-group/manchester-united-plc-and-trawlers-ltd-announce-the-successful-completion-of-sir-jim-ratcliffes-minority-investment/ |website=ineos.com |date=20 February 2024 |access-date=2 August 2024 }}</ref>

[[Erik ten Hag]] began the campaign in his third year as manager, but was dismissed in October following a poor start to the season. Former United striker and assistant coach [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]] assumed interim charge before [[Rúben Amorim]] was appointed as head coach on 11 November, following his departure from [[Sporting CP]].

The season was widely regarded as the worst in the club's modern history. United finished 15th in the Premier League with 42 points—their lowest league position since [[1989–90 Manchester United F.C. season|1989–90]] and fewest points in a top-flight season since they were last relegated in [[1973–74 Manchester United F.C. season|1973–74]]. In domestic cup competitions, their defence of the FA Cup ended in the fifth round with a penalty shootout defeat at home to [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], while they were eliminated from the EFL Cup in the quarter-finals after a 4–3 loss to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. United reached the [[2025 UEFA Europa League final|final of the UEFA Europa League]], but were beaten 1–0 by Tottenham at the [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés Stadium]] in [[Bilbao]]. As a result, they failed to qualify for European competition for the first time since the [[2013–14 Manchester United F.C. season|2013–14]] season (and only the second time since [[1989–90 Manchester United F.C. season|1989–90]]). It was the club's first trophyless campaign since [[2021–22 Manchester United F.C. season|2021–22]].

==Pre-season and friendlies==
[[File:Williams-Brice Stadium, Manchester United v. Liverpool, 8-3-2024.jpg|thumb|Action from the pre-season game against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in [[South Carolina]].]]
On 23 February 2024, United announced a tour of the United States, with [[Exhibition game#Club football|friendly matches]] against rivals [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at the [[SoFi Stadium]] in [[Inglewood, California]] (near Los Angeles), on 27 July and at the [[Williams–Brice Stadium]] in [[Columbia, South Carolina]], on 3 August, respectively.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tour 2024: United to play Arsenal and Liverpool in USA |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-announce-tour-2024-games-v-premier-league-rivals-arsenal-and-liverpool-in-united-states |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=23 February 2024 |access-date=8 May 2024 }}</ref> In March, they announced another game in the United States – against [[Real Betis]] on 31 July at the [[Snapdragon Stadium]] in [[San Diego]], a venue with which the club shares a sponsor.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tour 2024: United to play in San Diego again |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-announces-tour-2024-pre-season-game-v-real-betis-in-san-diego-usa |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=12 March 2024 |access-date=8 May 2024 }}</ref> Ten days later, United announced they would play [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] for the first time in a decade at [[Murrayfield Stadium]] in Edinburgh on 20 July.<ref>{{cite news |title=United v Rangers: tickets now on sale |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-to-play-rangers-in-edinburgh-friendly-in-july-2024 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=22 March 2024 |access-date=8 May 2024 }}</ref> The first match of their pre-season tour was announced on 5 April; they faced Norwegian side [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] at the [[Lerkendal Stadion]] in Trondheim on 15 July.<ref>{{cite news |title=United v Rosenborg: get your tickets now |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-to-open-pre-season-with-friendly-v-rosenborg-in-trondheim |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=5 April 2024 |access-date=8 May 2024 }}</ref>

United lost their first match of pre-season against Rosenborg 1–0 after a goal in the last minute.<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Carney |title=Match report: Rosenborg 1 United 0 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-for-man-utd-v-rosenborg-friendly-in-norway-15-july |website=ManUtd.com |date=15 July 2024 |access-date=2 September 2024 }}</ref> They registered their first win of pre-season in Scotland, where they beat Rangers 2–0 thanks to goals from [[Amad Diallo]] and [[Joe Hugill]]; newly signed defender [[Leny Yoro]] made his debut in the game, playing the first 45 minutes.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Higgins |title=Match report: Rangers 0 United 2 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/rangers-v-man-utd-match-report-and-video-highlights-20-july-2024 |website=ManUtd.com |date=20 July 2024 |access-date=2 September 2024 }}</ref> In the first game of the U.S. tour against Arsenal, [[Rasmus Højlund]] put United ahead early; however, both he and Yoro suffered injuries in the first half that ruled them out of the opening matches of the season. [[Gabriel Jesus]] levelled in the first half and [[Gabriel Martinelli]] scored the winner for Arsenal after the break, although United went on to win the post-match exhibition penalty shoot-out 4–3.<ref>{{cite news |title=Match report: Arsenal 2 United 1 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-arsenal-v-man-utd-pre-season-tour-27-july-2024 |website=ManUtd.com |date=27 July 2024 |access-date=2 September 2024 }}</ref> United returned to winning ways against Real Betis, when goals from [[Marcus Rashford]], Amad Diallo and [[Casemiro]] secured a 3–2 win.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Bostock |title=Match report: United 3 Real Betis 2 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/real-betis-v-man-utd-pre-season-match-report-san-diego-tour-2024 |website=ManUtd.com |date=1 August 2024 |access-date=2 September 2024 }}</ref> Manchester United's tour of the United States ended with a 3–0 loss to [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] Liverpool.<ref>{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Ganley |title=Match report: United 0 Liverpool 3 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-man-utd-v-liverpool-tour-2024-south-carolina-3-august-2024 |website=ManUtd.com |date=4 August 2024 |access-date=2 September 2024 }}</ref>

At the end of the season, Manchester United travelled to Asia to play friendlies against an [[ASEAN All-Stars]] team in Kuala Lumpur and the [[Hong Kong national football team|Hong Kong national team]] in Hong Kong.<ref>{{cite news |title=United to visit Kuala Lumpur and Hong Kong in May |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-to-visit-kuala-lumpur-and-hong-kong-in-may-2025 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=8 April 2025 |accessdate=8 April 2025 }}</ref>

==FA Community Shield==
{{main|2024 FA Community Shield}}
As a result of winning the [[2023–24 FA Cup]], Manchester United faced [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], who won the [[2023–24 Premier League]], in what was United's 31st [[FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] appearance, and their first since [[2016 FA Community Shield|2016]].<ref>{{cite news |title=2024 FA Community Shield date, kick-off time and TV details are confirmed |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2024/jun/26/community-shield-date-kick-off-time-confirmed-20242606 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=26 June 2024 |accessdate=26 June 2024 }}</ref> After United took the lead late in the second-half through [[Alejandro Garnacho]], City equalised through [[Bernardo Silva]] in the 88th minute, taking the game to penalties. [[André Onana]] saved City's first penalty from Silva, but [[Jadon Sancho]]'s miss with United's fourth kick meant the shoot-out went to sudden death; [[Jonny Evans]] put United's eighth penalty over the bar, allowing [[Manuel Akanji]] to give City a 7–6 victory.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man Utd 1-1 Man City LIVE: Manuel Akanji scores winner as Man City beat Man United 7-6 on penalties in Community Shield, reaction, stats & updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c9wjkjyqpg4t |website=BBC Sport |date=10 August 2024 |accessdate=14 August 2024 }}</ref>

==Premier League==
{{Main|2024–25 Premier League}}

===Matches===
The [[2024–25 Premier League]] fixtures were released on 18 June 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=Revealed: United's 2024/25 Premier League fixtures |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-premier-league-fixtures-2024-25-revealed-global |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=18 June 2024 |access-date=18 June 2024 }}</ref> Manchester United opened their Premier League campaign on 16 August 2024 with a 1–0 win over [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]]. Substitute and debutant [[Joshua Zirkzee]] scored the only goal of the match in the 87th minute.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cr40634rz5wt |title=Man Utd 1-0 Fulham: Zirkzee scores late winner on debut as Man Utd beat Fulham in opener |website=[[BBC Sport]] |date=16 August 2024 |access-date=21 August 2024}}</ref> United then travelled to the Amex Stadium to take on [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]]. Former United man [[Danny Welbeck]] opened the scoring in the 30th minute, capitalising on a defensive mistake. [[Amad Diallo]] then levelled the scores in the 61st minute, before United put the ball in the back of the net again through [[Alejandro Garnacho]]; however, replays showed that Zirkzee had accidentally tapped the ball into the net from an offside position while attempting to stand up, causing the goal to be ruled out. [[João Pedro (footballer, born 2001)|João Pedro]] then scored a late winner with an unmarked header at the back post, condemning the Red Devils to a first league defeat of the season. United then hosted [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|arch-rivals]] [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at home; although United started well, [[Trent Alexander-Arnold]] had the ball in their net in the 8th minute, although the goal was ultimately ruled out for offside. By half-time, United found themselves 2–0 down due to a brace of goals from [[Luis Díaz (footballer, born 1997)|Luis Díaz]]. [[Mohamed Salah]] scored a third goal for Liverpool in the 56th minute to seal a 3–0 defeat for United.

United then travelled to [[St Mary's Stadium]] to face newly promoted [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]]. Two first half goals from [[Matthijs de Ligt]] and [[Marcus Rashford]] in quick succession, after United goalkeeper [[Andre Onana]] had been forced into a penalty save, meant the game was comfortable for United. Garnacho then came off the bench to score a third in second half stoppage time, securing a second victory of the season. United's next game against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] was a 0–0 draw, where Onana gained his third clean sheet of the season after being forced into a double-save that later won [[Premier League Save of the Month]] for September. To close the month, the Red Devils hosted [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], and they conceded in the third minute after centre-back [[Micky van de Ven]] was allowed to run through the midfield unchallenged before setting up [[Brennan Johnson]] to score. [[Bruno Fernandes]] was sent off for the first time in his career after a late tackle on James Maddison, leaving United with 10 men just before half-time. The second half was marked by goals from [[Dejan Kulusevski]] and [[Dominic Solanke]], sealing a second 3–0 defeat at home in a row.

To kick off October, United traveled to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. An exemplary performance from defender [[Jonny Evans]] helped secure a clean sheet, though Villa's keeper and Man of the Match [[Emiliano Martínez]] held United to a goalless draw.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Aston Villa 0-0 Manchester United: Erik ten Hag's side earn battling draw at Villa Park |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cdjerlny927t |website=BBC Sport |date=6 October 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> This result left United with their worst start since the 1989–90 campaign.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title='We are on one page' - Ten Hag believes he still has Man Utd backing |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c20m5686p0go |website=BBC Sport |date=6 October 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> Two weeks later, following the international break, United hosted [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]]. The visitors opened the scoring when [[Ethan Pinnock]] headed in a corner in the fifth minute of stoppage time at the end of the first half. Garnacho equalised for United two minutes after the restart, before [[Rasmus Højlund]] scored in the 62nd minute to win the game 2–1.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United vs Brentford: Premier League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cp95eg5dpdzt |website=BBC Sport |date=19 October 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> For the last Premier League game of October, United were away to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]]. After a goalless first half, West Ham opened the scoring in the 74th minute through [[Crysencio Summerville]]. United were able to equalise in the 81st minute through a header from [[Casemiro]], only for a penalty to be awarded late on for a collision between Matthijs de Ligt and [[Danny Ings]] inside Man Utd's penalty area; although it was not given on the field, a VAR check ultimately awarded West Ham a penalty. [[Jarrod Bowen]] scored from the spot in injury time to win the game for West Ham.<ref>{{cite news |title=Late Bowen penalty gives West Ham win against Man Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c9wrj7dzzxlt |website=BBC Sport |date=27 October 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> This was manager [[Erik ten Hag]]'s last game as Man Utd manager, as on 28 October it was announced that he had been sacked, and that [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]] would take over as the interim manager.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Simon |last1=Stone |first2=Sean |last2=Kearns |title=Man Utd sack manager Ten Hag |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cpvznn4v01yo |work=BBC Sport |date=28 October 2024 |access-date=28 October 2024}}</ref> 
For the first game of November, United hosted [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. United opened the scoring in the second half, with Rasmus Højlund being taken down in the box by Chelsea goalkeeper [[Robert Sánchez]] with Bruno Fernandes subsequently converting the penalty. The lead did not last long, however, as just four minutes after scoring, [[Moisés Caicedo]] scored an equaliser with a volley from the edge of the box following a corner. The game ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Manchester United 1-1 Chelsea: Ruud van Nistelrooy's first Premier League game in charge ends in draw |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm271r8ljy2t |website=BBC Sport |date=3 November 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> United then hosted [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] and opened the scoring in the 17th minute through a Bruno Fernandes shot at the edge of the box into the bottom right corner. United scored again in the first half in the 38th minute as [[Noussair Mazraoui]] crossed in the ball, with it deflecting off both Bruno Fernandes and Leicester defender [[Victor Kristiansen]] into the Leicester net, going down as a Kristiansen own goal. To close the game, substitute Alejandro Garnacho scored a screamer from outside the box curling the ball into the top right corner, winning the game 3–0 for Man United.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man Utd 3-0 Leicester City: Bruno Fernandes shines in Premier League win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c1lgj2eje9vt |website=BBC Sport |date=10 November 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> United's first game under newly appointed head coach [[Ruben Amorim]] came after another international break and saw them travel to [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]]. United opened the scoring after just 90 seconds through Marcus Rashford, but were unable to hold onto their lead, as in the 43rd minute, Ipswich's [[Omari Hutchinson]] scored from a shot outside the box, deflecting off the head of Mazraoui into the top left corner of the goal. Neither side was able to convert their chances in the second half and the game ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Ipswich Town 1-1 Manchester United: Ruben Amorim's era begins with draw at Ipswich |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c0en20qjjv8t |website=BBC Sport |date=24 November 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref>

To open December, United hosted [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]. United won comfortably 4–0 with Rashford and Zirkzee both scoring twice.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Manchester United vs Everton: Premier League preview, team news, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ckglqgrwgx0t |website=BBC Sport |date=1 December 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> The following game was away against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who won 2–0 through goals from [[Jurriën Timber]] and [[William Saliba]], both coming from corners.<ref>{{cite news |first=Alex |last=Howell |title=Arsenal 2-0 Man Utd: Defeat for Ruben Amorim as William Saliba and Jurrien Timber score goals for Gunners |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx2l21kvdlpt |website=BBC Sport |date=4 December 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> United then hosted [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] at Old Trafford. Forest centre back [[Nikola Milenković]] opened scoring in just the second minute from a corner. Rasmus Højlund was able to equalise in the 18th minute, scoring a rebound after Garnacho had his shot saved by Forest goalkeeper [[Matz Sels]]. Early in the second half Forest took the lead again through [[Morgan Gibbs-White]] scoring from outside of the box. [[Chris Wood (footballer, born 1991)|Chris Wood]] then added to Forest's lead, scoring a looping header in the 54th minute. In the 61st minute, Bruno Fernandes scored a goal from the edge of the box, but United were unable to convert any of their other chances, and the game finished 3–2.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man Utd 2-3 Nottingham Forest: Chris Wood strikes as Ruben Amorim suffers home Premier League defeat |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g2dzj47z1t |website=BBC Sport |date=7 December 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> It was the first time Forest had beaten United at Old Trafford since December 1994.<ref>{{cite news |title=First win at Old Trafford since 1994 a huge moment for Forest, Nuno says |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/first-win-old-trafford-since-1994-huge-moment-forest-nuno-says-2024-12-08/ |work=Reuters |date=8 December 2024 |access-date=23 January 2025 }}</ref> Next was the [[Manchester derby]] away at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]]. City opened the scoring in the first half through a [[Joško Gvardiol]] header. Late on in the game, Amad Diallo intercepted a poor back-pass from [[Matheus Nunes]], who brought Amad down inside the box, earning a penalty for United. Bruno Fernandes successfully converted the penalty to bring the game level. Less than two minutes later, a long ball over the top found Amad, who took the ball around [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] with his first touch and scored with his second touch, winning the game 2–1 for Manchester United.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man City 1-2 Man Utd; Amad Diallo scores late winner as visitors come from behind to stun champions |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c1j0x0p890lt |website=BBC Sport |date=15 December 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> Following this, United hosted [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]]. In the first half, United conceded from another set-piece as [[Dean Huijsen]] scored a flicked header from a [[Ryan Christie]] free-kick. In the second half, Noussair Mazraoui brought down [[Justin Kluivert]] in the box to concede a penalty, which Kluivert scored. Just two minutes after the penalty, [[Antoine Semenyo]] scored the final goal and United lost 3–0 at home to Bournemouth for the second season in a row.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United vs AFC Bournemouth: Premier League preview, team news, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwy3590ynxyt |website=BBC Sport |date=22 December 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> On Boxing Day, United travelled to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] where, early in the second half, captain Bruno Fernandes was sent off for a second yellow card. In the 58th minute, [[Matheus Cunha]] scored directly from a corner to give Wolves the lead. In the ninth minute of injury time, [[Hwang Hee-chan]] scored to end the game in a 2–0 defeat for United.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Wolves 2-0 Manchester United: Matheus Cunha scores from corner in win over 10-man Red Devils |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c8xj1xrxvy9t |website=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref> For the last Premier League game of 2024, United hosted [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]], who scored twice in the opening 20 minutes through [[Alexander Isak]] and [[Joelinton]], ending the year with a 2–0 loss for Manchester United.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 0-2 Newcastle United: Alexander Isak scores again as visitors claim dominant win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c0j1571xqj2t |website=BBC Sport |date=31 December 2024 |accessdate=1 February 2025 }}</ref>

On 19 January 2025, Amorim labelled his team as probably the worst in the history of the club after their 3–1 defeat to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]]. The defeat was the club's fourth in the past five games at [[Old Trafford]]. Following the defeat, the club sat in 13th in the table, 10 points above the relegation zone.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester United 1-3 Brighton: Ruben Amorim says this is 'maybe the worst team in Man Utd history' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c77r85gj45xo |website=BBC Sport |date=19 January 2025 |access-date=20 January 2025 }}</ref>

By mid-May with two Premier League games remaining United had slipped to 16th place in the league following a 2–0 defeat to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] at Old Trafford, which marked their ninth home league defeat of season (a joint club record) and their seventeenth defeat in the league overall. This also meant the club equalled its worst winless run in the Premier League era of seven league games without a win.<ref>{{cite web | title=Manchester United vs West Ham United: Premier League preview, team news, stats & head-to-head | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c77n7v4z7ext }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Optus Sport Has Closed | url=https://sport.optus.com.au/news/premier-league/os92790/manchester-united-terrible-premier-league-season-west-ham-old-trafford-loss }}</ref> This winless run in the league was extended to record 8 games after United suffered a 1–0 defeat to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] in their penultimate Premier League fixture.<ref>{{cite web | title=Chelsea 1-0 Manchester United: Marc Cucurella scores winner in Premier League game | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cr58md2d428t }}</ref> United ended their winless run in the league after beating [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] 2–0 at Old Trafford in the final league match of season courtesy of goals from Amad Diallo and Christian Eriksen. This meant United finished 15th in the league table with 42 points, that  points total being just half that of bitter rivals and eventual champions [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Manchester United 2-0 Aston Villa: Controversy as Villa miss out on Champions League on final day | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cvgvvkegl42t }}</ref>

==FA Cup==
Manchester United went into the [[2024–25 FA Cup]] as defending champions. For the first time, drawn games in all rounds from the First Round Proper onward were not [[Replay (sports)|replayed]], instead proceeding straight to [[overtime (sports)|extra time]] and [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Emirates FA Cup format updated for 2024-25 |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2024/apr/18/emirates-fa-cup-format-calendar-update-increased-premier-league-grassroots-funding-20241804 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=18 April 2024 |accessdate=14 August 2024 }}</ref>

==EFL Cup==
As one of the English representatives in European competition in 2024–25, Manchester United entered the [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] in the third round, which took place over two midweeks due to the extended European league phases. As United are in the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]], their tie was played in the week commencing 16 September. None of the clubs involved in the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] or Europa League could be drawn against each other.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=New-look Carabao Cup round-three draw details 2024 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/new-look-carabao-cup-round-three-draw-details-2024 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=26 August 2024 |accessdate=27 August 2024 }}</ref> United were drawn against [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] in the third round to set up a first meeting in 15 years,<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Carney |title=Man Utd discover Carabao Cup opponents |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-discover-carabao-cup-third-round-opponents-for-september-2024 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=28 August 2024 |access-date=29 August 2024 }}</ref> which they comfortably won 7–0.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-man-utd-v-barnsley-carabao-cup-17-september-2024 |title=Match report: Man Utd 7 Barnsley 0 |first=Adam |last=Higgins |publisher=Manchester United |website=ManUtd.com |date=17 September 2024 |access-date=10 November 2024 }}</ref> In the fourth round, they were drawn at home against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Draw made for Carabao Cup Round Four |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2024/september/25/draw-made-for-carabao-cup-round-four/ |access-date=26 September 2024 |publisher=English Football League |date=25 September 2024}}</ref> This was [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]]'s first match as interim manager that they won 5–2.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-man-utd-leicester-carabao-cup-fourth-round-2024 |title=Match report: Manchester United 5 Leicester City 2 |first=Adam |last=Marshall |publisher=Manchester United |website=ManUtd.com |date=30 October 2024 |access-date=10 November 2024 }}</ref> They were drawn away against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=United discover quarter-final opponents |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/carabao-cup-2024-25-quarter-final-draw-details |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=30 October 2024 |access-date=30 October 2024 }}</ref> United lost the match 4–3 and were eliminated.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-for-tottenham-v-man-utd-carabao-cup-quarter-final |title=Match report for Tottenham v Man Utd |first=Sam |last=Carney |publisher=Manchester United |website=ManUtd.com |date=19 December 2024 |access-date=7 January 2025 }}</ref>

==UEFA Europa League==
===League phase===
Manchester United qualified for the league stage of the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] as winners of the [[2023–24 FA Cup]]. This is the competition's first season with a new format; United played eight games, four at home and four away, against eight different teams.<ref>{{cite news |title=Race for European football ends with Man Utd qualifying for Europa League and Newcastle missing out |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13143017/race-for-european-football-ends-with-man-utd-qualifying-for-europa-league-and-newcastle-missing-out |website=Sky Sports |date=25 May 2024 |accessdate=30 January 2025 }}</ref> After drawing their first three games, United won their remaining five to finish third in the league table and qualify directly for the round of 16 as the only remaining undefeated team in the League phase.<ref name="whats_next">{{cite news |title=Who is through in Europa League and what's next? |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cj91y18xynko |website=BBC Sport |date=30 January 2025 |accessdate=31 January 2025 }}</ref>

===Knockout phase===
As one of the top eight teams from the league phase, United qualified directly for the round of 16.<ref name="whats_next"/><ref>{{cite news |title=UEFA Europa League round of 16 draw: Real Sociedad get Manchester United, AZ Alkmaar welcome Tottenham, Roma draw final hosts Athletic Club |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0296-1d1c40b7d6b5-2d329d036222-1000--uefa-europa-league-round-of-16-draw-real-sociedad-get-manch/ |access-date=21 February 2025 |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=21 February 2025}}</ref> In the knockout phase, United saw off [[Real Sociedad]] on aggregate in the Round of 16; secured a dramatic comeback victory against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] 7-6 on aggregate after extra time in the quarter-finals, having been at one stage on the brink of elimination; and comfortably beat [[Athletic Bilbao]] in 7-1 on aggregate the semi-finals to set up a meeting against fellow Premier League side [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in the final of the competition in Bilbao on 21 May 2025.<ref>{{cite web | title=The official website for European football | url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0295-1cf0ec0a866d-66d44dcc4421-1000--europa-league-meet-the-finalists/ }}</ref> In [[2025 UEFA Europa League final|the final]] United would lose 1-0 to Tottenham thanks to goal from Spurs winger [[Brennan Johnson]] in the 42nd minute, meaning United had lost to Spurs in all four of the meetings between the respective clubs across all competitions during the 2024-25 season and as a result of losing this particular match would not play in any European Football competition the following season for the first time since the [[2014–15 Manchester United F.C. season|2014–15 season]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Tottenham 1-0 Man Utd: Brennan Johnson goal seals Europa League win for Spurs & ends 17-year wait for trophy | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cz9yney9391t }}</ref>
